pathway_hypotheses.title: MTAP-associated methionine-salvage and methylation vulnerability
pathway_hypotheses.patient_specific_basis: The tumor is reported to have MTAP DNA copy-number loss and RNA underexpression. These are supportive but do not establish homozygous deletion, absent protein, or a functionally MTAP-null state.
simplified_pathway: MTAP normally metabolizes methylthioadenosine within the methionine-salvage pathway.
Functionally complete MTAP loss can cause methylthioadenosine accumulation and alter methylation-pathway biochemistry.
That biochemical state may create context-dependent dependence on PRMT5-pathway or related metabolic functions.
This dependency cannot be inferred in this patient until complete MTAP loss and its biochemical consequences are confirmed.
potential_vulnerabilities: Investigational dependency associated with confirmed MTAP-null status
Potential PRMT5-pathway dependence, contingent on complete MTAP loss and relevant pharmacodynamic evidence
potential_bypass_or_escape_routes: Residual MTAP activity from heterozygous loss or incomplete protein suppression
Metabolic compensation that prevents sufficient methylthioadenosine accumulation
Pathway adaptation downstream of PRMT5 or related methionine-cycle processes
Intratumoral heterogeneity in MTAP deletion or protein expression
potential_combination_or_recombination_p: Mechanistic and investigational hypothesis: pair an MTAP-context dependency approach with a second intervention only where preclinical evidence demonstrates complementary stress and acceptable therapeutic index; this is not a treatment recommendation.
Mechanistic and investigational hypothesis: evaluate whether the cell-cycle abnormalities in this case modify MTAP-associated dependency, without assuming synergy from genomic proximity alone.
